key_insight: WEST is a scalable open-source platform for excited-state simulations that combines GW, Bethe-Salpeter, TDDFT, and related methods without explicit virtual states.
engineering_relevance: Its low-rank algorithms, localization strategies, and GPU-enabled hierarchical parallelization make high-accuracy excited-state modeling practical for large materials systems, including perovskites.
method: Full-frequency GW, quantum defect embedding, BSE, and TDDFT in one framework
Avoids explicit virtual-state sums using density-functional and density-matrix perturbation theory
Uses low-rank dielectric/exact-exchange representations plus strong GPU scaling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports near-ideal strong scaling to thousands of GPUs and successful simulations of systems with more than a thousand atoms across multiple representative materials.
watch_item: Performance and workflow interoperability may depend on specialized HPC/GPU resources and careful setup of the coupled excited-state methods.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
